boundaryReview.finding: The Node branch never constructs the old Effect body stream before the native adapter. It forwards raw bytes as a stream, with no JSON transformation, full buffering, retry or synthetic response. GET/HEAD omit the body; other methods set duplex half. Native backpressure is pause/resume through desiredSize and the readable high-water mark.
The candidate adds no grant, actor binding, domain mutation, persistence shortcut or alternate business handler. It does not prove that installed authorization or persistence succeeds.

The real Effect.tryPromise signal is still attached to the final Request passed to installation.handler. Preserving Request.signal does not establish that an arbitrary pending body reader terminates, or that cancellation reaches the underlying IncomingMessage promptly.

The body lifecycle changes from Effect readable.read/latch plus scope finalization to native data/pause/resume/finished/cancel. Native cancel destroys the Node source, and native completion still depends on source terminal events. There is no new explicit completion-time cancellation in the candidate. Empty/partial bodies, terminal error, disconnect and pending-body cancellation remain unproven.

An early response after construction may leave an unread body. The review cannot infer that listeners are released or that the next keep-alive request remains intact; test actual early rejection followed by another request without weakening domain authorization.

No body-limit constant or downstream parser is edited. The inspected existing Effect stream path does not itself show the MaxBodySize enforcement used by its text/arrayBuffer readers. Do not claim either a new global cap regression or global chunked cap preservation from declared Content-Length rejection alone; validate the actual bounded product readers and declared oversized-body gate.

The helper throws on an absent toURL result within the existing route catchCause; the503 fallback and403 origin gate remain. Privacy, mount pattern, original dispose and host contributions remain unchanged. No body, identity or header logging is added.
